name: kelmar
author: weather-and-seasons designer
description:
kelmar (direction: weather and seasons) -- RAIN SHOWERS OVER A GARDEN ROW: THE PLANTS
STANDING JUST OUTSIDE THE RAIN. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = "<ground>/*<a>Y<b>". <ground> is one row of bare earth "_" 42-52 columns wide with
5-8 flowers "*" and 4-7 small trees "Y" planted on it, never closer than 3 columns apart
and never in the outermost two columns. a and b are 1..3 with a+b<=5, a <= flowers-3 and
b <= trees-3 (so the digits are never the number of plants of that kind, and there are
always spare plants of both kinds).

SOLUTION = a picture of rain falling on that garden. The scorer keeps the non-blank lines,
right-strips them, and requires the LAST one to be the clue's ground row verbatim. Every
line above it is a sky row: "#", "|", "/" and "'" all read as rain, space, "." and "_" as
dry sky, anything else is rejected. There must be at least two sky rows and they must all
be IDENTICAL (the rain falls straight down), each as long as the ground row. Every maximal
run of rain ("a shower") must be at least 3 columns wide, consecutive showers must be
separated by at least 2 dry columns, and there must be at least 2 showers. Labels, blank
lines, indentation with spaces, 2-4 sky rows and any of the rain glyphs are all free.

THE RULE: exactly a FLOWERS and exactly b TREES stand in a column immediately to the left
or immediately to the right of a shower -- dry, right at the edge of the rain, just missing
it. Wet plants never count, plants two or more columns clear never count. Nothing else is
checked: which plants they are, how many showers, how wide, how wet the rest of the garden
is, are all free.

INTENDED PATH: one demo gives the whole grammar (the clue is the bottom line); the only
question is what the two digits count. Round 2-3 is spent on "how many get rained on",
"how many stay dry", "how many showers" -- all of which every shipped demo falsifies -- and
the crack is the sentence a 12-year-old says while pointing: "that one is standing right on
the edge of the shower and staying dry".

DEGENERATE WITNESSES CLOSED (measured, 250 fresh clues, attackers that know the grammar
perfectly and build a legal picture satisfying their own hypothesis): random legal picture
6.8 %, best blind sampler over 15 density settings 12.4 %, "rain on a of them / b of them"
(the natural first probe) 7.6 %, "a stay dry" 4.8 %, "at the last WET column" (the near
miss) 4.8 %, "beside rain, wet or dry" 1.2 %, "two columns clear" 5.6 %, "showers with one
under them" 6.4 %, one big shower 3.6 %, regular stripes 7.2 %, one fixed picture for every
clue 6.0 %, previous clue's answer 0.0 %, junk/empty/clue echoed 0.0 %. The two readings
that DO pay are both the intended insight: counting showers-with-a-plant-at-their-edge
instead of plants 86 %, and the rule with the two glyphs not told apart 47.6 %.

solve() picks a target plants and b trees, hangs showers so that exactly those stand at an
edge, then hill-climbs on decoy showers until every rival statistic above differs from the
clue's digits AND the picture also shows: a plant on a shower's last wet column, a plant two
columns clear of the rain, a plant deep inside a shower, a plant far from any rain, and a
shower that catches nobody. 85 % of demos meet all of that; the rest miss one item. Layout,
rain glyph, dry glyph, sky height (2-4) and shower count all vary between demos, so no demo
is a template for the next.
score:
def score(c,s):
 g,k=c.split("/");W=len(g)
 L=[x.rstrip()for x in s.split("\n")if x.strip()]
 if len(L)<3 or L[-1]!=g:return 0
 P={re.sub("[#|/']","1",re.sub("[ ._]","0",x.ljust(W)))for x in L[:-1]}
 p=P.pop()
 if P or len(p)!=W or set(p)-set("01"):return 0
 R=[m.span()for m in re.finditer("1+",p)]
 if len(R)<2 or any(b-a<3 or(i and a-R[i-1][1]<2)for i,(a,b)in enumerate(R)):return 0
 E=[g[i]for a,b in R for i in(a-1,b)if 0<=i<W]
 return int(E.count("*")==int(k[1])and E.count("Y")==int(k[3]))
